answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to first complete an auditable task whose output peers can re-run, before that identity may vote or be paid. From the terrace of earned history, an operator cannot cheaply clone a thousand wallets, because every clone must supply its own verified work. Reputation then grows like a reef, slow and publicly inspectable, and each fresh identity must carry its own lantern of proof, so a sybil fleet costs real labour per seat instead of a scripted loop.
